thread.title: Tech Today: Amazon Fizzles, Intel Shines, Microsoft Rebounds - Barron's

title: Tech Today: Amazon Fizzles, Intel Shines, Microsoft Rebounds - Barron's
text:
Updated April 27, 2018 11:01 a.m. ET
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Pre-market gains for some of the leaders in tech have fizzled in the past hour despite impressive earnings results.
Amazon Gives Up Some Gains
Shares of Amazon.com ( AMZN ) are up $60.26, or almost 4%, at $1,578.22, giving up some of last night’s gains. The company yesterday afternoon comfortably beat Q1 expectations for revenue and profit, and forecast revenue this quarter in line but guided profit higher than the Street has been estimating, as Jon Swartz wrote .
Amazon’s market capitalization of $784 billion, based on 498 million shares outstanding, is closing in on Apple ’s ( AAPL ) $817 billion market cap, as Jon pointed out in a separate post.
There are no ratings changes today, that I can see, but price targets are creeping up into the $2,000 range.
$2,000 is the target Daniel Salmon with BMO Capital assigns, up from $1,700. He notes it was the second-most-profitable quarter in Amazon’s history, and he gives a lot of credit for it to Amazon’s growing advertising business , which he now thinks will make $9.5 billion in revenue this year, way up from his prior forecast for $6.9 billion.
Salmon thinks Amazon can “easily” make $1 trillion worth of gross merchandise sales come 2020. And he now assigns a value to Amazon’s Web Services cloud-computing operation of $300 billion.
Intel Makes Bears Think Again
Another winner from last night is Intel ( INTC ), after it comfortably beat Q1 expectations and offered a forecast that positively crushed the consensus. The company also raised its year revenue outlook to $67.5 billion from $65 billion, and raised its EPS outlook to $3.85 from $3.55.
But the stock has given up a 6%-or-so jump last night; it's now up just 29 cents at $53.34.
There are numerous price-target increases today, and one upgrade, from Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein , who raises his rating to Market Perform from Underperform.
Among price target increases, Needham & Co. ’s Quinn Bolton , who has a Buy on the stock, raises his target to $62 from $50, writing that all the parts of Intel’s server-chip business, “Data Center Group,” increased in the quarter, including chips for networking equipment, which were up 33%, in part because of sales in advance of deployment of 5G wireless networks . The cloud computing chip products saw sales rise by 45% thanks to Intel’s Xeon chip.
For the beleaguered bears, Bernstein’s Rasgon, who was banking in part of weakness in data center chips, writes that "the recent unexpected DCG inflection has made it painful ” to be skeptical.
"Given CFO Bob Swan does not like to put out numbers he cannot hit, we suspect 2H visibility might be better than they are letting on,” Rasgon concludes of the company’s forecast data center will rise “in the upper teens."
FormFactor Is Intel Collateral Damage
There is some collateral damage, however: Intel said last night it will further delay the ramp of its 10-nanometer chip production from the second half of this year to 2019.
That prompts Bolton’s colleague Edwin Mok to cut his rating on chip-equipment maker FormFactor (FORM) to merely a Buy from what had been a Strong Buy rating, after concluding the push-out of 10-nano will cut revenue for FormFactor’s “probe” cards for semiconductor testing.
He still advises buying the stock, on the premise that lots of DRAM memory chips going into smartphones need to be tested, even in a weaker smartphone market.
Formfactor shares are down $2.07, or 15%, at $11.68.
The further delay in Intel’s manufacturing should be music to the ears of Lisa Su , CEO of competitor Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ). Read my interview with Su yesterday .
AMD stock is up 15 cents, or 1.4%, at $11.19.
Microsoft Rebounds
One weaker showing yesterday was Microsoft ( MSFT ), whose shares sagged in after-hours trading despite a fiscal Q3 revenue and earnings beat. But once the conference call got underway, and CFO Amy Hood forecast revenue this quarter topping the Street consensus, the shares turned around.
This morning, Microsoft is up 31 cents at $94.57, amidst numerous price-target increases this morning.
It also got one upgrade, that I can see, from J.P. Morgan ’s Mark Murphy , who raises his rating to Overweight from Neutral, with a $110 price target, up from $94, writing that the company is poised to benefit from a “global multi-cloud” movement in cloud computing, and more broadly from “digital transformation initiatives."
T-Mo and Sprint for Real?
Shares of Sprint ( S ) are up 43 cents, or 7%, at $6.43, and T-Mobile US ( TMUS ) is up 97 cents, or 1.5%, at $65.07, as talks heat up between the two for a merger .
Reuters reported last night that the companies "have made progress in negotiating merger terms and are aiming to successfully complete deal talks as early as next week,” citing multiple unnamed sources.
Wells Fargo analyst Jennifer Fritzsche writes that a deal “Seems more real to us this time."
She notes in particular one of the nuggets in the Reuters report, that Deutsche Telekom ( DT ), parent of T-Mobile US, "could consolidate the new combined company on its books (and here is the key) 'even without owning a majority stake.’"
"That is a significant statement if true,” she writes, given its challenges "the accepted belief that DT (which owns 63% of TMUS) would need to own the majority."
"If this was the case, and the assumed ratio was paid, it would value S at no more than ~ $6. If the ratio is the same--but DT is not the majority owner of the stock-then that would imply S would be valued at a higher price."
